page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute and memory workflows. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 are fully supported alongside cryptographic instruction extensions.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance characteristics. The server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded operations, including stress-ng single-core performance and gzip compression tests. Multi-core execution ranks in the middle tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 18686.8 and balanced multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput. Memory bandwidth measures 49.09 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 33.83 GB/sec for write tasks. Lightweight inference workloads perform well, demonstrating upper-quartile token generation speeds on small 135M language models, while heavier prompt processing on 7B models demonstrates weaker execution speeds typical of CPU-only instances.

Architecturally, the D8as_v7 does not include bundled local disk storage or attached GPUs, requiring reliance on remote persistent storage configurations. This setup limits applications requiring ultra-low-latency ephemeral swap or scratch disks, but maintains qualitative infrastructure cost efficiency by eliminating expenditures on unused NVMe disks. The instance is suited for general enterprise workloads, static web serving, intermediate caching layers, standard database applications, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D8as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with x86_64 architecture. The system provisions 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading at 4.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM at a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 vector extensions, 32 MB of L3 cache, and dedicated hypervisor scheduling under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides no integrated local storage and contains zero GPUs, focusing resources on compute density and memory availability. Benchmark results show top-tier single-threaded CPU and compression throughput, alongside mid-tier memory bandwidth and multi-core execution metrics. Caching performance reaches 13.66 million Redis SET operations per second, with web serving throughput delivering 15.73 GB/sec. The instance delivers a cost-efficient profile for moderate multi-threaded tasks, enterprise application hosting, microservices, mid-sized relational database operations, and continuous integration runners.
